author: Nthambeleni M
title: Extremely Disappointing Service and Lack of Follow-Up from Discovery
review: I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with the level of service I have received from Discovery. Some time ago, I lodged a formal complaint regarding the service I was receiving from my then-broker. I was subsequently informed that the broker was no longer employed by Discovery and that a new broker would be allocated to assist me. However, months have passed, and not a single person has contacted me. There has been absolutely no follow-up, no communication, and no indication of when I can expect assistance. I urgently need to review my portfolio, yet I have been left completely in the dark despite having raised my concerns through the appropriate channels. It is incredibly stressful and unacceptable to have to continuously worry about matters that should be handled efficiently by a company of Discovery's stature. What is the point of lodging a complaint and being assured that the matter will be attended to if no action is taken thereafter? The lack of communication and accountability is deeply concerning and reflects very poorly on Discovery's customer service. I should not have to chase Discovery for months just to receive the assistance I was promised. I expect Discovery to take this matter seriously, allocate a competent and responsive broker to my portfolio, and arrange an urgent review of my portfolio. I am genuinely exhausted and stressed by this experience. Discovery needs to do better. Customers deserve to be treated with respect, their concerns addressed timeously, and promises made to them honoured. I would appreciate an urgent and meaningful resolution to this matter, not another empty assurance. If u can't assist please do let me know so I can go to other service providers like PPS, I think they will be happy to offer me a better services

author: Susan B
title: FUEL PURCAHSE NOT CONFIRMED DESPITE PROOF AND REPEATED FOLLOW-UPS
review: I am extremely disappointed with Discovery Insure's handling of my fuel purchase query and the contradictory information I keep receiving. On 4 November 2026, I purchased fuel for R964.72. I paid cash and swiped my physical Vitality card. I routinely submit my fuel receipts because previous purchases were not reflected on Discovery's system, resulting in me losing out. During this query, Discovery first advised me that my insurance policy had lapsed, which was incorrect. After that issue was resolved, a representative claimed that I had not swiped my card for the fuel purchase. I sent the receipt again, with the relevant transaction details circled to show that the card had been swiped. She subsequently called to apologise and acknowledged that she had overlooked this information. Another Discovery representative confirmed during a recorded telephone call that the new system would take effect on 1 December 2026 and that swiping the physical card remained valid until that change. All I have requested is written confirmation that my fuel purchase of 4 November 2026 has been correctly registered. Instead, I have now received an email stating that the card-swiping method is no longer valid, has expired, and that they cannot check the transaction. This contradicts what I was told. I have asked for my complaint to be escalated, but I have received no satisfactory resolution. I should not lose a fuel benefit because of Discovery's internal problems or contradictory guidance when I followed the process explained to me. I require Discovery Insure to: Escalate this complaint to a manager who can resolve it. Review my receipt and the recorded telephone conversations. Confirm in writing whether the R964.72 fuel purchase has been registered. Correct any omission and ensure that I receive any benefit due under my policy. References: ***; ***; ***; ***. The repeated errors, contradictory responses and lack of resolution are unacceptable. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Discovery Insure.

author: kurt F
title: DISCOVERY INSURE: Authorised Repairs Using Wrong-Vehicle Part Numbers & Unilaterally Closed Claim!
review: I am posting this urgent public warning regarding severe claims maladministration and bad-faith file handling by Discovery Insure (Claim Number: ***). After three months of delays, an on-site physical audit conducted on 6 November 2026 by Ronwic Motors and William Simpson BAIC—cross-checked across Mekor and Group1 BAIC—exposed a shocking truth: the Netassess assessment report Discovery used to calculate my payout and authorize repairs contained completely incorrect part numbers and pricing . When I formally challenged this and submitted the manufacturer's findings to the National Financial Ombud Scheme (NFO Case ***), Discovery's claims desk did not resolve the error. Instead: 1. Netassess refused to defend their flawed report and escalated the crisis to Discovery's senior management on 12 November 2026. 2. Discovery's portal generated a system error ("exceeds mandate of 150000.00") alongside *******ed authorization documents. 3. On 13 November 2026, Discovery unilaterally marked my claim "Finalised" on my online profile and removed my live tracking view—forcing my repairer to refund my parts deposit because the assessment data is unusable, and leaving my 9-month-old BAIC Beijing X55 un-repaired with no transport ahead of the December shutdown. This matter is currently before the NFO Adjudicator, where I am demanding a binding Total Loss Write-Off under my Classic Plan's 12-month New Vehicle Replacement benefit, alongside full restitution for my out-of-pocket losses. Consumers deserve transparency and safe, manufacturer-compliant claims handling—not administrative abandonment.
